name: Cooly Eco Adventures
summary: Small-group whale swims, whale watching, turtle snorkelling and dolphin and turtle safaris from Chinderah on the Tweed River, near the New South Wales and Queensland border. Trips run on a 32ft open ocean boat with seating for 12 guests. Whale season runs from June to November, and August to October is the best time to swim with whales.
standouts: States it was the first operator on the Gold Coast to offer swimming with whales
Small groups: a 32ft open ocean boat seating 12 guests, and a maximum of 9 swimmers in the water on whale swims
Whale and turtle sightings from the boat are guaranteed, or you return for free
Home page shows Sustainability Awards Winner 2025 and Best of Queensland Experience 2026 badges

contact.address: 139 Chinderah Bay Dr, Chinderah NSW 2487 (departure point)

trips.title: Swim with Whales
trips.summary: A swim with humpback whales, run from Chinderah on the Tweed River on a 32ft open ocean boat. No more than 9 swimmers are in the water at a time, each group with an experienced guide. The operator guarantees whale sightings from the boat but not a swim, because the whales decide whether to join the group.
highlights: Maximum 9 swimmers in the water with an experienced guide
In-water approach as close as 30 metres, then it is up to the whale
Swim and snorkel gear and wetsuits provided
All photos and videos of the trip included
trips.season: Whale season June to November; best time to swim with whales is August to October
trips.departsFrom: 139 Chinderah Bay Dr, Chinderah NSW 2487 (look for the big trailer parked along the river)
includes: Qualified, experienced skipper and crew
Maximum 9 swimmers in the water, accompanied by an experienced guide
Swim and snorkel gear (mask, fins, snorkel), wetsuits and reef safe sunscreen
In-water crew support and flotation devices available
Commentary on humpback whales, other marine life, Aboriginal and European history and the local area
All photos and videos of the trip
Fresh fruit after the swim
bring: Beanie and a warm jumper or jacket
Spray jacket or rain coat (basic ponchos are provided)
trips.requirements: Minimum age 15; anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Must be able to swim unassisted, and snorkelling experience is necessary. Not suitable for pregnant women or anyone with a back injury.
trips.checkNotes: Price, times and duration are from the tour page. Two departure times (6:30am and 11am, weather and tide dependent) are listed, yet the same page says only one whale swim tour runs a day, in the early morning; check which is right. Operating dates are not stated: the tour page says whales migrate May to November, the FAQ says June to November, with August to October best for swimming. The page says a swim is not guaranteed; Terms clause 5.5 allows a free rebook within 12 months if no whales are seen from the boat. The page offers flotation devices and in-water support, while Terms clause 2.6 says swimmers must swim unassisted without a buoyancy aid. The page also makes a first-operator claim and gives its sighting guarantee as a percentage; the percentage is not repeated here. The Rezdy link on the page carried a PHPSESSID session id, which was removed; the Rezdy page was not opened.

trips.title: Whale Watching
trips.summary: A small-group whale watching trip from Chinderah on a 32ft safari-style open ocean boat with room for 12 guests, so everyone watches from close to eye level. An on-board naturalist talks about whales and ocean conservation, and eagles, dolphins, turtles and flying fish may also be seen. The operator guarantees whale sightings from the boat, or you return for free.
highlights: On-board naturalist commentary on whales and ocean conservation
Departs via the Tweed River to the Pacific Ocean
trips.season: Whale season June to November (best time to see whales, per the FAQ)
trips.departsFrom: 139 Chinderah Bay Dr, Chinderah NSW 2487 (look for the big trailer parked along the river)
includes: Whale sighting guarantee, or return for free
Small groups, up to 12 passengers per tour
Experienced, knowledgeable crew
Commentary from an on-board naturalist on whales and ocean conservation
Coastline and wildlife viewing, with the possibility of eagles, dolphins, turtles and flying fish

trips.title: Swim with Turtles
trips.summary: A guided snorkel with sea turtles at Cook Island Aquatic Reserve, about 600 metres off Fingal Head, reached by a 20 minute boat ride from Chinderah. A maximum of 12 swimmers are in the water at a time with an experienced guide, and snorkel instruction is given. The operator guarantees turtle sightings from the boat, or you return for free.
highlights: 20 minute boat ride to Cook Island Aquatic Reserve
Maximum 12 swimmers in the water with an experienced guide
Wetsuit, mask, snorkel and fins provided

trips.checkNotes: Prices, times and duration are from the tour page; the page says tour times are subject to change with tide and wind. Minimum age 6 comes from the Terms and Conditions (the tour page gives only the child price band of 6 to 12 and says under 18s need a parent or guardian). The tour page says previous snorkelling experience is not necessary, while the Terms list snorkelling experience as necessary (that line looks written for the whale swim); the tour page was used. The page gives a sighting guarantee and a chance of swimming with turtles as percentages; they are not repeated here. No operating season is stated. The Rezdy link on the page carried a useTransparentSessions query, which was removed; the Rezdy page was not opened.

trips.title: Dolphin & Turtle Safari
trips.summary: A boat trip to watch turtles and dolphins from a 32ft open ocean boat carrying up to 12 passengers. It heads out through the Tweed River entrance to Cook Island Aquatic Reserve, then follows the Fingal Head and Tweed Heads coast looking for dolphins. The operator guarantees turtle sightings, or you return for free.
highlights: Cook Island Aquatic Reserve, then the Fingal Head and Tweed Heads coast
Dolphin and turtle watching from the boat

offers.text: Sighting guarantee: whale sightings from the boat on the Swim with Whales and Whale Watching tours, and turtle sightings on the Swim with Turtles and Dolphin & Turtle Safari tours, are guaranteed or you return for free

checkNotes: All four tours are read from their own pages on the operator's site, and every Book Now button on those pages points to a Rezdy page under coolyecoadventures.rezdy.com; no Rezdy page was opened. Prices are in Australian dollars and include GST where applicable (Terms clause 4.2), and the Terms say the full amount is paid when booking on the website. State and town: all trips leave from Chinderah NSW (contact page and every tour page), but the Terms name a Queensland-based trustee company (LTA Investments Pty Ltd, ABN 71 705 693 549) and Queensland law, and the list says Gold Coast; NSW follows the departure address. The address shown is the departure point, not a postal address. Conflicts: the FAQ page says to see mothers and calves in September or October, while the other pages say late October and November; whale season is May to November on the tour pages and June to November in the FAQ. Copyright: the Terms (Part B, clause 2) say all images, logos and designs are owned by the operator and may not be reused without written authorisation, so get the operator's consent before publishing their photos. The site banner and Terms mention percentages (a flash sale, sighting rates, emission claims) that are not repeated here; the sustainability claims on the site (emissions, hydrogen fuel system) were left out because they are the operator's own unverified figures. No gift card purchase link was found. The award badges are known only from image descriptions on the home page (Sustainability Awards Winner 2025, Best of Queensland Experience 2026, and a Tweed Business Awards logo with no result shown), so check what each one says before using them. Customer review names and quotes on the pages were not used. The contact page form has a CAPTCHA field but every page loaded normally and no bot check was met.
